process.pageTagline: Between a dew-covered leaf on the mountain and the taste in your cup lie a dozen or so steps. This page takes them apart one by one — including the trade-offs we make along the way.

experienceCta.title: Experience the Tea Mountain
experienceCta.tagline: Reading about it is one thing. Step into our Ali Mountain tea gardens and work through it yourself, from plucking to finished leaf — you will not drink tea quite the same way afterwards.

pick.name: Plucking
pick.desc: We head up at first light and hand-pick the leaves while they still carry their dew. Maturity sets the backbone of the batch: too tender and the liquor comes on strong but turns bitter, and it is difficult to process; too mature and it turns coarse and thin. One bud with three to four leaves is where we draw the line, and every shoot is judged by the picker, one at a time.
pick.detail: How we judge it: by how far the bud has opened, not by the date on the calendar. Even a single plot gets picked in stages.

witherSun.name: Sun Withering
witherSun.desc: The leaves are spread outdoors on clean cloth to release moisture. The cell structure softens, and the first aromatics are drawn out right here, in the sun. This step follows the weather, not the clock: strong sun means a thicker spread; an overcast day means spreading thinner, or simply taking longer.
witherSun.detail: Duration: 20 minutes to a little over an hour, adjusted according to sunlight and temperature. How we judge it: when the leaf surface loses its sheen and feels supple rather than brittle, it comes indoors.

witherIndoor.name: Indoor Withering
witherIndoor.desc: The leaves move indoors, onto well-ventilated withering racks. In a temperature- and humidity-controlled room the moisture keeps working its way out, and the maker turns the leaves at intervals so every one of them loses it evenly. Less happens here than anywhere else in the process, and yet this is where the foundation of the aroma is built. It cannot be rushed.
witherIndoor.detail: Duration: 8–12 hours, temperature maintained at 18–26°C. How we judge it: when the raw green note fades into a clean fragrance and the leaf bends without snapping.

shake.name: Tossing
shake.desc: The decisive step in oolong. The maker tumbles the leaves so their edges bruise against one another, and oxidation starts at those breaks — the enzymes wake up, and the floral and fruity notes that belong to this tea begin to form. Toss lightly and the oxidation stays light; toss hard and it runs deep. Whether an oolong ends up delicate or full-bodied is settled right here.
shake.detail: Frequency: once every 1.5–2.5 hours, repeated 2–4 times. How we judge it: by how much of the leaf edge has turned red and how the aroma is shifting; every round is reassessed before the next.

fix.name: Fixation
fix.desc: Once oxidation has reached the point we want, the leaves go into a drum fixation machine, tumbling continuously inside a hot rotating cylinder. The enzymes are deactivated and oxidation stops on the spot; the grassy note is driven off, a toasted one takes its place, and the aroma is fixed where it stands. This is the brake pedal of tea making — whatever flavour this batch has reached is locked in at this moment, and there is no going back.
fix.detail: Equipment: drum fixation machine. Temperature: 260–300°C, duration: approximately 5–8 minutes. How we judge it: when the grassy note turns toasted and a handful of leaves feels soft without sticking, it comes off the machine.

roll.name: Rolling
roll.desc: Straight off the machine and still warm, the leaves are wrapped in cloth and rolled — tightening into balls or strands while the juices are worked onto the leaf surface. That coating is the point: in the pot the leaves open readily, and the flavour comes out whole.
roll.detail: Rolled continuously for 3–5 minutes. How we judge it: when the leaves have formed strands and feel tacky in the hand without weeping.

ferment.name: Oxidation
ferment.desc: After rolling breaks the cell walls, the leaves are left to oxidise fully on their own. This stage belongs to the black teas: with no fixation to stop it, oxidation runs to completion, catechins convert, the liquor turns red and the honey note emerges.
ferment.detail: How we judge it: leaf colour shifting from green to red-brown and the aroma turning from green to honeyed. That is the only instrument panel we have here.

dryFirst.name: First Drying
dryFirst.desc: A type-A dryer brings the moisture down and holds the tea steady so it stops changing. After first drying the leaf is still loose — it takes the rolling that follows to become a ball.
dryFirst.detail: Equipment: type-A dryer. How we judge it: the leaf no longer sticks to the hand but still keeps its give; it must not be dried brittle.

ballRoll.name: Cloth Ball Rolling
ballRoll.desc: The tea is wrapped in cloth, drawn into a ball, tightened in a press, then opened and broken up — and then it starts again. Wrap, roll, break, repeat, several passes over, until the leaves knot into a semi-ball. Those tight little spheres you see in the bag are ground out one pass at a time.
ballRoll.detail: Equipment: press and cloth ball rolling. How we judge it: by tightness and shape, repeating until it holds.

dryFinal.name: Drying & Stem Sorting
dryFinal.desc: Once the shape is set the tea is dried down to a keeping moisture level, and sorting happens at the same time: long stems are pulled out by a coarse sorter, and a blower lifts away debris and substandard leaf. Drying and sorting are one operation, not two.
dryFinal.detail: Equipment: coarse sorter for long stems, blower for debris and substandard leaf. How we judge it: the leaf snaps cleanly instead of bending back, and stem separates freely.

roast.name: Roasting
roast.desc: Primary processing finishes at the factory; roasting happens back home, adjusted slowly in a cabinet roaster. Roasting shapes flavour — it brings sweetness and body, steadies the batch, and shores up whatever that lot is short on. Push it too far and the floral top notes and freshness are gone, so it can only ever be roasted to the right point. Every batch comes out a little different, and roasting is our last chance to tune it to what a customer wants. Everything listed online comes at a set roast level; if you want a specific roast, ask us in the shop or by message.
roast.detail: Temperature: 70–120°C, duration: 4–16 hours depending on style. Equipment: cabinet roaster. How we judge it: the flavour this particular batch is carrying, and what the customer is after.

pack.name: Packaging
pack.desc: As soon as the flavour has landed the tea is packed — nothing is reworked after this. Vacuum-sealed foil shuts out light and air, holding the batch at its best moment until you open it.
pack.detail: Every batch is labelled with the tea name, origin and other details.

ferment.skipReason: Fixation has already stopped oxidation, so there is no separate oxidation stage — this is exactly where oolong and black tea part ways.

roast.desc: High mountain oolong is made both roasted and unroasted. Everything listed online is lightly roasted — for the added sweetness, body and consistency. The unroasted version keeps its freshness and floral lift, but it depends on how a given batch turns out and the yield is unpredictable, so it is only offered in the shop or on request, never listed online.
roast.detail: Temperature: 70–120°C, duration: 4–16 hours depending on style. How we judge it: whether to roast at all depends on the flavour this batch is carrying; everything sold online is lightly roasted, with unroasted available on request.

ferment.skipReason: Fixation has already stopped oxidation, so there is no separate oxidation stage.

pick.desc: Four Seasons is machine harvested — cut by a harvester rather than hand-selected to the one-bud-three-or-four-leaves standard. Machine harvesting costs far less than picking by hand, and combined with an early-budding cultivar that can be picked several times a year, that is where the affordable price comes from. A different harvesting method, not a compromise on quality.
pick.detail: Harvesting method: machine. It costs far less than hand picking, and together with several harvests a year it is the structural reason Four Seasons is affordable.

ferment.skipReason: Fixation has already stopped oxidation, so there is no separate oxidation stage.

roast.skipReason: Four Seasons is not roasted at all — it is sold unroasted, because its unroasted floral freshness is the whole point. Generally only green-style oolongs can go without roasting.

pick.desc: Honey black tea is plucked under a stricter condition than the others: the leaves must first have been bitten by the tea green leafhopper. The bush responds with a defence reaction, and that is where the honey note comes from — so here the leafhopper is a requirement rather than a problem, while other pests and diseases are still managed as usual.
pick.detail: How we judge it: whether the leaves show signs of leafhopper bite. No bite, no honey note.

shake.desc: The decisive step for this black tea. The maker tumbles the leaves so their edges bruise against one another, and oxidation starts at those breaks — the enzymes wake up, and the floral and fruity notes that belong to this tea begin to form. Toss lightly and the oxidation stays light; toss hard and it runs deep. Whether this black tea ends up delicate or full-bodied is settled right here.

fix.skipReason: Honey black tea skips fixation. Without that brake, the leaves can oxidise all the way through and finish as a black tea.

roll.desc: Day one follows the oolong path of withering and tossing; day two switches to black tea processing, starting with rolling to rupture the cells and release the juices so full oxidation can follow. The order is the reverse of oolong — oolong fixes then rolls, this rolls first, because there is no fixation at all.
roll.detail: How we judge it: rolled until the cells are thoroughly broken and the juices show, or oxidation will not run to completion.

ferment.desc: After rolling, the leaves rest and oxidise fully — the heart of this tea. The honey note earned from the leafhopper bite is released here and the liquor turns bright red. Once oxidation is done it goes back to the oolong press and cloth ball rolling, which is why this is a ball-rolled black tea: two traditions joined end to end.
ferment.detail: How we judge it: stopped when the leaf turns red-brown and the honey note is unmistakable.

witherIndoor.desc: Red oolong gets a noticeably longer indoor withering than the others, so moisture works through more completely and the groundwork for heavy oxidation goes deeper.
witherIndoor.detail: How we judge it: taken further than a standard oolong, watching suppleness and how far the aroma has turned.

shake.desc: The tossing is far heavier than a standard oolong, bruising more of the leaf edge so oxidation runs faster and deeper. The 'red' in red oolong starts here.
shake.detail: How we judge it: a markedly higher proportion of red leaf edge than a standard oolong.

roll.desc: Red oolong rolls the way a black tea does: rolling comes first, rupturing the cells and releasing the juices, and the leaves are then left to rest and oxidise. The order is the exact reverse of an oolong — oolong fixes then rolls; red oolong rolls, then oxidises, and only then is fixed.
roll.detail: How we judge it: rolled until the cells are thoroughly broken and the juices show, or the heavy oxidation will not run deep.

ferment.desc: Heavy oxidation is what gives red oolong its name, taken almost to black tea levels, and it is where the fruit and honey character forms. The first two steps here — rolling, then oxidation — run in the same order as honey black tea, the difference being that red oolong stops the oxidation short. What actually separates them is the fixation that comes after.
ferment.detail: How we judge it: taken close to black tea depth, but stopped before it gets there.

roast.desc: Red oolong is heavily roasted. Heavy oxidation followed by a heavy roast pulls the fruit character in towards honey and builds body and consistency — a completely different temperament from the lightly roasted teas.
roast.detail: Temperature: 70–120°C, duration: 4–16 hours depending on style. Equipment: cabinet roaster. How we judge it: roasted until the fruit note turns honeyed and the liquor feels full.

divergence.commonOpeningTitle: Shared Opening — Day One at the Factory
divergence.commonOpeningDesc: All five teas are identical to this point: picked, withered, tossed. Nothing has diverged yet.
divergence.divergenceTitle: The Divergence — Where the Five Teas Split
divergence.divergenceDesc: Every difference comes from these three slots. What matters is where fixation sits: first makes an oolong, absent makes a black tea, last makes a red oolong.
divergence.commonClosingDesc: The divergence ends and all five teas return to the same equipment: first drying, ball rolling, drying and sorting, roasting, packing. Even the black tea goes through this, which is why it too is ball-rolled.
divergence.insightTitle: The Difference Is Only in the Middle
divergence.insightDesc: Rather than five separate processes, this is one road that forks in the middle. Understand the divergence and you understand Taiwanese tea.

partialBall.name: Partially Oxidised, Ball-Rolled
partialBall.desc: Fixation comes first and oxidation is stopped early. High mountain oolong, Jin Xuan and Four Seasons all belong here.

fullBall.name: Fully Oxidised, Ball-Rolled
fullBall.desc: No fixation at all — oxidation runs to completion, yet it still finishes on the ball-rolling line. Unique to honey black tea.

heavyBall.name: Heavily Oxidised, Ball-Rolled
heavyBall.desc: Oxidised heavily first, with fixation held back to the very end. Red oolong's signature move.

sourcing.note: Every tea is made where that tea belongs.

teaSelector.label: Pick a tea to see how it is made
teaSelector.hint: Switching teas only changes the middle section.

matrix.title: All Five Teas, Side by Side
matrix.desc: Every difference in one table. Scroll sideways to see all columns.

craftNote.title: Why It Is Done This Way
craftNote.oolong: There are more variables at altitude, so oolong depends more on craft — get the technique right and the quality holds steady. Our processing facility is not beside the tea garden but in a spot with plenty of sun, which makes sun withering straightforward. As for flavour, the weather shifts it a little from year to year: close, but genuinely not identical.
craftNote.jinxuan: Jin Xuan is only ever lightly roasted — a light roast does not remove the milky note. It takes a medium roast to turn it buttery, and that is not a loss, just a change of form; only a heavy roast buries it under the roast character.
craftNote.sijichun: Four Seasons is affordable for two structural reasons, chiefly machine harvesting — it costs far less than picking by hand — combined with an early-budding cultivar that can be picked several times a year. That is a difference in cost structure, not a compromise on quality. Songboling is Taiwan's main Four Seasons region, and this tea is made there.
craftNote.black: Made as an oolong on day one, as a black tea on day two, then returned to the oolong press and cloth ball rolling — it is two traditions joined together. The honey note comes from the bush's defence response to leafhopper bites, so what this tea needs is for the leafhoppers to stay; other pests and diseases are still managed as usual.
craftNote.redOolong: It is still fixed after heavy oxidation, and that is the line between it and a black tea — oxidation is paused rather than finished, keeping the oolong sweetness. Luye is where red oolong originated, and this tea is made there.
craftNote.roastNote: Primary processing at the factory, refining back home on a cabinet roaster — this is how the division between primary and refined processing actually works in Taiwan. Roasting is a trade: you gain sweetness, body and consistency, and if you push too far you lose the floral top notes and the freshness. Admitting that cost is more honest than calling it 'carefully roasted'.

productCta.label: Buy this tea
productCta.hint: You have seen how it is made. Now taste it.

meta.title: Tea Craftsmanship
meta.description: A side-by-side look at how all five teas are made — high mountain oolong, Jin Xuan, Four Seasons Spring, honey black tea and red oolong. All five share the same opening and closing steps; the difference is the branch in the middle: pan-firing first makes an oolong, no pan-firing makes a black tea, and pan-firing last makes a red oolong.
meta.ogDescription: Five teas walk the same road and part ways only in the middle. Once you see where pan-firing sits, you understand how Taiwanese tea is classified.

hero.title: Behind every cup is the sincerity and dedication of our family of three

story.title: Alishan Meishan — A Family Tea Garden Story
story.p1: Our parents entered the tea industry when they were young, and for over 40 years we have tended our gardens in the Alishan Meishan tea region with love and dedication. Wu Jue Tea has always stood for growing and selling our own tea.
story.p2: From growing and processing to roasting, packing, and shipping — every step is handled by our family of three. Every cup you hold is the result of time and heart.
story.p3: All so you can enjoy that smooth, sweet sip with complete peace of mind.

gallery.tagline: From the early morning harvest to the late-night roast — capturing every precious moment in a tea leaf's transformation

selfGrown.title: Farm to Cup
selfGrown.desc: From growing to shipping, every step is personally overseen by our family of three. No middlemen — just our guarantee of quality and freshness in every pack.

heritage.title: 40 Years of Craft
heritage.desc: Over 40 years since our parents first entered the tea industry. Our roasting is guided by decades of accumulated experience and trained intuition — every batch is a labor of love.

region.title: Alishan Meishan Tea Region
region.desc: Our gardens sit in the Alishan Meishan mountains of Chiayi, Taiwan. The cool highland climate and year-round mist give our teas their distinctively sweet, mellow flavor.

jinxuan.name: Jin Xuan Tea

black.name: Black Tea

sijichun.desc: Known for its lively wild floral aroma. Bright green liquor with a fresh, sweet taste and long-lasting fragrance — an ideal everyday tea companion.

hero.label: Privacy Policy
hero.title: Privacy Policy
hero.tagline:
Wu Jue Tea values your personal data security and privacy.
Please read the following carefully.

s1.title: 1. Purpose of Personal Data Collection
s1.content:
This website (Wu Jue Tea), in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act, collects necessary personal data when you use our services for the following purposes:

• Order processing and fulfillment: including name, phone number, email, and shipping address, used for order confirmation, shipment arrangement, and order notifications.
• Customer service: handling return/exchange requests, inquiries, and after-sales service.
• Newsletter and marketing communications (with your explicit consent only): occasional notifications about new products and promotional offers.

We will not use your personal data for purposes beyond those stated above without your consent.

s2.title: 2. Scope of Personal Data Usage
s2.content:
Personal data collected by this website is used only within the following scope:

• Providing the products or services you requested.
• Sending order-related notifications (order confirmation, shipping updates).
• Processing your payments (through ECPay payment platform; we do not store your credit card information).
• Complying with legal requirements or requests from judicial/administrative authorities through legal procedures.

We will not sell, rent, or otherwise provide your personal data to any third party, except for logistics providers and payment service providers necessary for order fulfillment, and only to the extent required to complete the order.

s3.title: 3. Personal Data Protection Measures
s3.content:
This website employs appropriate technical and administrative measures to protect your personal data:

• The website uses HTTPS encryption to ensure data security during transmission.
• Order data is stored in a cloud database (Supabase) with security protections and access controls.
• Payment processing is handled through the ECPay payment platform; we do not store any credit card or financial account information.
• Our staff may only access customer personal data when necessary for their duties.

In the event of a personal data breach, we will notify affected individuals in accordance with the law.

s4.title: 4. Cookie Policy
s4.content:
This website uses cookies and similar technologies to improve user experience:

• Essential cookies: necessary for basic website functions such as shopping cart and login status.
• Analytics cookies (if applicable): to understand how visitors use the website and help improve content and features.

You may refuse or delete cookies through your browser settings, but this may affect the normal operation of certain website features.

s5.title: 5. Your Rights
s5.content:
Under Article 3 of the Personal Data Protection Act, you have the following rights regarding your personal data held by this website:

• Right to inquire or request access: You may inquire about the personal data we hold about you at any time.
• Right to request copies: You may request copies of your personal data.
• Right to supplement or correct: You may request corrections if your personal data is inaccurate or incomplete.
• Right to request cessation: You may request that we stop collecting, processing, or using your personal data.
• Right to request deletion: You may request that we delete your personal data.

To exercise these rights, please contact us by phone (0972-619-391) or email (qdbzdt2846@gmail.com). We will respond within 15 business days.

If exercising these rights incurs necessary costs, we may charge a reasonable fee. If your request is unreasonable, excessively repetitive, or abusive, we may refuse or charge a reasonable fee in accordance with the law.

s6.title: 6. Data Retention Period
s6.content:
This website retains personal data for the following periods:

• Order-related data: 5 years from order completion (per Consumer Protection Act and tax regulations).
• Customer service records: 2 years from case closure.
• Marketing mailing lists: until you unsubscribe, or when we cease marketing activities.

After the retention period expires, we will destroy or de-identify the data in accordance with the law.

s7.title: 7. Third-Party Links
s7.content: This website may contain links to third-party websites. We are not responsible for the privacy policies or content of those websites. We recommend reviewing their privacy policies before visiting.

s8.title: 8. Privacy Policy Amendments
s8.content:
This website reserves the right to amend this privacy policy at any time. Updated policies will be posted on this page. For significant changes, we will notify you prominently (such as posting on the homepage or sending an email). We recommend reviewing this policy periodically.

This privacy policy was last updated on January 1, 2026.

hero.label: Return Policy
hero.title: Return & Exchange Policy
hero.tagline:
We want you to be satisfied with every purchase.
Please contact us if you have any questions.

section1.title: 7-Day Inspection Period
section1.content: Under Article 19 of the Consumer Protection Act, you have a 7-day cooling-off period after receiving your product, during which you may request a return without stating a reason.
section1.noteContent: The inspection period is a "reasonable period for examining the product," not a trial period. Products should remain in new, unopened condition. Please do not open or use the product before requesting a return, as this may affect your return rights.

s1.desc: Within 7 days of receiving your product, call 0972-619-391 or email qdbzdt2846@gmail.com with your order number, return items, and reason.

s2.desc: We will confirm your return eligibility and arrange the return process within 2 business days.

s3.desc: Please return the product with its original packaging, any gifts, and the invoice. Return shipping is paid by the customer; if the product is defective or was shipped incorrectly, we will cover the shipping cost.

s4.desc: After we receive and verify the returned product, we will arrange a refund within 3 business days.

m1.label: Credit Card Payment
m1.desc: Refunds will be returned to the original credit card account. Processing takes approximately 7–14 business days depending on your bank.

m2.label: Cash on Delivery
m2.desc: Refunds will be issued via bank transfer. Please provide your bank details (bank name, branch, account number, account holder). Refunds will be processed within 3 business days after return confirmation.

section4.title: Return Exceptions
section4.intro: Under Article 19, Paragraph 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, the 7-day inspection period does not apply in the following cases:

exceptions.e1: Product has been opened (tea and food products cannot be returned once opened due to hygiene and safety concerns)
exceptions.e2: Product is damaged, soiled, or missing parts due to non-defect-related causes
exceptions.e4: Product has deteriorated or been damaged due to improper use or storage
exceptions.e5: Product has been used or tried

section4.noteContent: Wu Jue Tea products are agricultural food products. To maintain food safety and hygiene, tea products cannot be returned or exchanged once opened. Please evaluate carefully before purchasing. If you notice packaging damage or obvious defects upon delivery, please take photos and contact us within 48 hours. We will arrange a replacement or refund as appropriate.
